outcomes: A reviewer reads the change summary on the pull request or merge request, not in the CI log, and one click on it reaches the full report of the change
A CI job adds --upload --publish to putnami observe with the tokens it holds, and gets a commit status and one summary note that link to the full report, updated in place by the next run
A job without an upload, a failed upload, a missing code host token, or a job outside a pull or merge request logs why it published nothing and still passes
nonGoals: Failing the commit status on a failed test or a low coverage: the status says the analysis ran
Code hosts other than GitHub and GitLab, and CI systems other than GitHub Actions and GitLab CI
Publishing on a branch push that has no pull or merge request

text: With --publish, putnami observe sets the commit status putnami/observe to success on the head commit of a GitHub pull request, or on the commit of a GitLab merge request pipeline, CI_COMMIT_SHA, joined to that pipeline.
Its description, at most 140 characters, counts the changed and dependent components, the changed-line coverage and the dependency changes, or says the base was not resolved.
Its target_url is the report URL the evidence reporter answered, else the CI run page.
With --publish, putnami observe writes one Markdown summary note on the pull or merge request whose first line is the hidden marker <!-- putnami-observe:summary -->.
The note keeps its summary, and its first link is the report URL the evidence reporter answered; without one it links the CI run page.
It updates the first note whose body starts with that marker and creates one when none does, so a second run updates the same note.
A failed status call does not stop the note.
--publish needs --upload: the note links the report the upload stored.
Without --upload, --publish gives the info observe.publish_needs_upload and sends no request.
When the upload fails, it gives the info observe.publish_skipped, which says the upload failed, and sends no request. putnami observe still exits 0.
On GitHub the token is GITHUB_TOKEN and the API is GITHUB_API_URL, https://api.github.com when unset.
On GitLab the token is PUTNAMI_GITLAB_TOKEN, a project or personal access token, and the API is CI_API_V4_URL, else CI_SERVER_URL followed by /api/v4, so a self-managed GitLab answers on its own URL.
The token goes only to an https API URL without credentials, redirects are not followed, and no token appears in a diagnostic or in the output.
--publish with an upload but without the code host's token gives the warning observe.publish_token_missing;
in a generic CI or outside a pull or merge request it gives the info observe.publish_skipped;

A refused or failed call, no GitLab API URL, an API URL that is not https, no commit to set the status on, or a run past one minute gives the warning observe.publish_failed. putnami observe still exits 0.
